Test file written: `tests/llm/test_persona_narration_cache.py`. It collects cleanly and runs offline in mock mode. Right now 36 tests fail and 8 pass; the 8 that pass cover Robert's unchanged modes and the checks that pass-status sections stay `template`, have no writer call and have no cache entry. The 36 failures are the expected ones: the Amira and Mateo sections still end in `template`, and the audit still lists `LLMCacheMiss` for `explainer.v2`. The other tests in `tests/llm` and `tests/test_d10.py` still pass, and I didn't edit any code outside `tests/`.

The tests use a module-scoped fixture that runs `pipeline.review` for Amira, Mateo and both Robert portfolios in a temp working directory. This is the same path `cli demo` takes.

- `test_demo_section_statuses_are_the_audited_ones`: Amira has horizon/contraintes violation and preferences info, and Mateo has contraintes unknown and preferences info. The other sections are `pass` (SPEC §16, §20.4).
- `test_every_non_pass_persona_section_ends_in_llm`: each non-pass section ends in mode `llm` with `verify.passed` true and no failures (SPEC §16, §20.5, §9.3).
- `test_pass_sections_stay_template_and_never_reach_the_writer`: `pass` sections are `template` and make no N5 call (§20.5).
- `test_report_and_audit_modes_agree_and_explanation_is_llm`: the audit `section_modes` match the report, and the overall explanation mode is `llm` (§10, §20.5).
- `test_no_explainer_cache_miss_left_in_the_audit`: no `explainer` errors or `LLMCacheMiss` in `llm_errors` (§10, §6.1).
- `test_one_hand_written_call_per_non_pass_section`: exactly one N5 call per non-pass section, model `fixture:hand-written`, `explainer.v2`, cache hit, accepted. Where `attempts` is recorded, it has one entry with no failures (§6.1, §9.3).
- `test_entry_is_keyed_like_robert_on_the_exact_section_facts`: the entry file exists under the real `cache_key`. Its payload is the facts unchanged, with no `retry_failures`, and it carries `hand_written: true` and the matching `input_hash` (§6.1, §16).
- `test_entry_output_is_schema_valid_and_passes_v1_to_v5`: the stored output validates against the explainer schema, `verify_section` returns no failures, and there are 1 to 4 segments. Each segment has refs, is at most 300 characters, and `numcheck` finds no number outside the facts (§9.2, §9.3, CLAUDE.md numbers rule).
- `test_entry_describes_never_prescribes`: no advisory wording on any segment or the joined text, and segment kinds stay within the allowed four (D10, §9.3 item 3, invariant 7).
- `test_entry_covers_every_failing_or_unknown_check`: every violation or warning check id is cited (V3). Every unknown check id is named in an `unknown` segment (§9.3). I picked the stricter reading for unknown checks and marked it with a `# SPEC-AMBIGUITY:` comment.
- `test_entry_is_a_hand_written_narration_not_the_template`: the stored segments differ from `template_section(facts)` (SPEC §16).
- `test_no_entry_exists_for_a_pass_section`: no hand-written entry is keyed on the facts of a `pass` section (§20.5).
- `test_robert_modes_are_unchanged`: Robert current has contraintes `llm` and everything else `template`. Robert + NVDA has horizon `llm`, risque `llm_retry`, contraintes `template`, and the rest `template` (§16, §20.5).
- `test_robert_nvda_contraintes_keeps_its_failure_trail`: Robert + NVDA contraintes stays `template` by design, and any recorded attempts are two rejected ones (§20.5).
